verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents Slack-centric incident running: Runbooks automatically create incident Slack channels, the default Runbook assigns the opener the Commander role, `/fh` works inside incident channels, and `/fh update` posts updates. However, declaring an incident from Slack is only implied, and Microsoft Teams appears only as a notification channel. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of declaring an incident from a Slack command, any Teams-based incident declaration or running, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an on-call engineer, I can declare and run an incident from chat — Slack or Teams — with channels, roles, and updates created for me

citations.quote: Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
Assigns whoever opened the incident to the Commander role.
From Slack, inside an incident channel, you can browse the list of triggered Runbooks for this by executing `/fh`.
All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
